skill.description: Turn user-provided personal finance records into a local interactive report with spending, income, transfers and cash movement in English or Chinese. Use for statement-based finance charts and period comparisons, not bank-account actions or investment advice.
skill.summary: Visualize reconciled personal finance records in local English or Chinese reports with transaction details and period comparisons.

content.user_title: Visualize Personal Spending and Cash Movement
content.value_statement: Personal finance records can obscure spending patterns when transfers, refunds, and shared expenses appear together. This skill guides reconciliation and renders local interactive reports with separate spending, income, transfer, and cash movement views.
actual_capabilities: Accept normalized JSON or CSV and validate transaction dates, amount signs, identifiers, currency, and source coverage.
Display spending, income, transfers, and adjusted external cash movement across daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly periods.
Apply confirmed personal expense shares, exact full-refund mappings, and partial transfer settlement allocations.
Provide interactive ring charts, area or bar timelines, and searchable transaction details with category and account filters.
Render English or Simplified Chinese interfaces with calendar navigation, keyboard controls, and rearrangeable chart layouts.
Serve reports from memory through a tokenized loopback URL, or create a standalone local HTML export on explicit request.
limitations: Raw bank exports require explicit field mapping; PDF extraction depends on authorized tools available in the agent environment.
Each report supports one currency with two decimal places; currency conversion and automatic partial-refund matching are not included.
The skill does not connect bank accounts, execute payments, modify subscriptions, or provide investment advice.
Local rendering does not prevent agent-host retention or browser traces; exported HTML embeds transaction details and requires private handling.

use_cases.title: Review Household Spending
use_cases.description: Separate shared housing costs, everyday purchases, and confirmed refunds to inspect personal spending without changing original bank amounts.

use_cases.title: Distinguish Income From Transfers
use_cases.description: Review confirmed salary or project income separately from internal account movements, unknown receipts, and external repayments.

use_cases.title: Compare Study Costs
use_cases.description: Compare supplied periods for housing, education, and everyday costs in English or Simplified Chinese while keeping missing coverage visible.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Fictional Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the bundled fictional finance demo in English. Open the local report without exporting a file or checking for updates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect the interface without supplying personal records.

prompt_templates.title: Review Normalized Transactions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my authorized normalized CSV for [period] in [currency]. Verify signs, coverage, and categories, then ask about unresolved items before rendering.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: create a report from prepared transaction data.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile Shared Costs and Refunds
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile my supplied records for [period]. Ask me to confirm personal shares, internal transfers, duplicates, and proposed refund matches before final charts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: resolve classification and reconciliation questions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Detailed Local Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Simplified Chinese report from my authorized JSON, including confirmed refund mappings and partial transfer settlements. Verify totals and transaction details. Export to [absolute local destination outside Git and the installed skill], without overwriting existing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: produce an explicitly requested private HTML export.

output_examples.input: Fictional USD records cover ten days with confirmed everyday expenses of $20, $30, and $50.
output: Daily living cost: $10.00 across ten covered days.
Transaction details retain all three original signed bank amounts.

output_examples.input: A fictional $84 purchase in February has a confirmed, exact $84 refund in March.
output: The matched purchase contributes $0.00 to February personal spending.
Bank-date cash movement retains the $84.00 February outflow and $84.00 March inflow.
The original purchase and refund remain available in transaction details.

best_practices: Confirm coverage, currency, amount signs, and duplicate evidence against the original records before reviewing charts.
Resolve uncertain classifications and relationships with the user; label any explicitly requested provisional results clearly.
Use account aliases and process stdin for newly normalized data; keep exports private and stop the local server after review.
anti_patterns: Treating every deposit as income or matching refunds and repayments using only similar names, dates, or amounts.
Combining different currencies without conversion evidence or presenting incomplete account coverage as a complete financial picture.
Publishing report links, exporting records without permission, or committing personal data and screenshots to a repository.

faq.question: What do I need to run the report?
faq.answer: You need Python 3.10 or later, a modern browser, and authorized normalized JSON or CSV records. A fictional demo is included.

faq.question: Can it read any bank statement automatically?
faq.answer: No. Raw CSV files need explicit column, sign, and date mappings. PDF extraction requires suitable authorized tools in your agent environment.

faq.question: Does financial reporting require an external connection?
faq.answer: The renderer uses local assets without external requests. A separate, user-requested update checker queries public GitHub release metadata without receiving financial records.

faq.question: Is my financial data completely erased after use?
faq.answer: No complete erasure is guaranteed. Agent-host retention, browser traces, and explicit exports can persist beyond the memory-only report server.

faq.question: How are shared costs, refunds, and repayments handled?
faq.answer: Confirmed shares affect spending only. Exact full refunds cancel purchase spending, while confirmed transfer settlements reduce adjusted transfer amounts without changing original bank records.

faq.question: Can I combine currencies or change the report language?
faq.answer: Use separate reports for different currencies; only two-decimal currencies are supported. The interface supports English and Simplified Chinese.
